page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the ARMv9 AWS Graviton architecture. The instance provides 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz using Neoverse-V2 cores. It features a per-core cache configuration of 64 KB L1 data cache and 2 MB L2 cache, supported by a shared 36 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is 32.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The instance lacks local instance storage, requiring remote EBS volumes for persistent data, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps with no included GPUs.

Benchmark results show balanced general compute capabilities with notable memory subsystem strength. The instance achieved a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3199.23 and demonstrated strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.48 GB/sec. Across standard compute benchmarks, performance sits largely within the middle 50 percent, delivering a Geekbench single-core score of 1895.0, a multi-core score of 10022.0, and 13645.93 on stress-ng multi-core testing. In-memory Redis SET throughput reached 19.17 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 19.89 GB/sec.

A hardware tradeoff appears in cryptographic and compute-heavy matrix operations. While hardware AES is supported, the PassMark encryption test scored in the bottom 25 percent, and medium 7B model prompt processing registered in the bottom 10 percent at 15.67 tokens per second. The lack of AVX or AMX vector extensions reflects its standard ARM ISA profile. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the architecture provides high memory throughput and full dedicated-core density without simultaneous multithreading overhead, making the m8gn.2xlarge appropriate for containerized microservices, caching layers, web serving, Clang compilation, and mid-tier enterprise application workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gn.2xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based cloud instance powered by 8 dedicated AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 physical cores clocked at 2.8 GHz. Configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio alongside a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. It includes no bundled local storage or discrete graphics accelerators, operating strictly with network-attached block volumes. Performance profiles highlight a top-tier memory subsystem with high uncached bandwidth and strong decompression rates, while overall CPU benchmarks like Geekbench and stress-ng place in the median range. Tradeoffs include lower encryption benchmark scores and constrained execution for larger LLM prompt processing. The instance is designed for balanced application demands such as microservices, Redis caching tiers, code compilation pipelines, and general web application hosting.
